## Design

### 2026-10-18 – I spent the majority of my week just 3D modeling the drive train. There wasn't much to it but it was my first time making one which is pretty challenging. I did learn some skills from a video, but I'm

**15h**

I spent the majority of my week just 3D modeling the drive train. There wasn't much to it but it was my first time making one which is pretty challenging. I did learn some skills from a video, but I'm not completely new to Onshape. I spent the first day drawing the sketch and setting everything up. I also put the measurements and dimensions down such as the screw size. After that, I extruded the sketch to get the first two plates of the model using the symmetric tool. I then projected that sketch and made another few adjustments before producing my next two plates in a similar manner. It was here that I first learned how to use the lighten tool. I had to download it from somewhere before I could use it so that took some figuring out to do. Then once the 4 plates were built, I got to work on assembly. I played around with the mate connectors, and I finally got the hang of it. The hardest part of all of this was being able to find how to import parts from a database. After guidance from a friend, I figured it out. The location was switched. After some experimenting, I got to work importing and connecting shafts and screws. I also learned how to make a screw through a certain tool that I believe is built into Onshape. I also made the pulley for the drive train which required a series of other steps as well as connecting it to the wheels which I imported. After abusing the replicating and fastening mate tool, I finally finished assembly. By then, my computer couldn't run very fast because the four wheels caused intense lag. However, I did finish and I look forward to making another one for our robotics team.

 (Also, sorry if the video isn't long for the reel, I didn't really know what to say and I kind of had to cram it into one draft.)
